newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel blames PFLP for West Bank attack.
newsitem.headline: Israel blames PFLP for West Bank attack.

text.p: Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai said on Wednesday that militants of George Habash's Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine (PFLP) killed two Jewish settlers in the West Bank.
"We know that those who carried out the attack were from the PFLP," Mordechai said at the West Bank Jewish settlement of Beit El, near where Wednesday's drive-by shooting occurred.
Mordechai, speaking at a hastily arranged news conference broadcast on Israeli radio and television, did not elaborate.

Wednesday was the anniversary of the founding of the PFLP in 1968. The PFLP along with Islamic movements Hamas and Islamic Jihad, opposes the Palestine Liberation Organisation's interim peace deal with Israel as a sell-out of the Palestinian cause.
The Israeli dead were a mother and her 12-year-old son, Israeli police and hospital officials said. Five other members of the family were wounded.
The family came under fire in their car by Arab gunmen from a passing vehicle near the Jewish settlement of Beit El outside the PLO-ruled Ramallah enclave, Israeli security sources said.
The Israeli army confirmed two Israelis were killed and five wounded.

The army said the attackers fled toward Ramallah. Israeli troops in coordination with Palestinian police had entered Ramallah to investigate an abandoned, torched car which fitted the description of the attackers' vehicle, Israel and the PLO said. Mordechai said the vehicle was the attackers' car.

A senior Palestinian official, speaking on condition of anonymity, had earlier told Reuters the Palestinian Authority condemned the attack and said it was aimed at weakening the PLO's negotiating position vis-a-vis Israel.

Netanyahu, speaking earlier to reporters at a Jerusalem hospital after visiting the wounded, said: "Whoever thinks that the Jewish people can be uprooted from its land, from the heart of the Jewish homeland by these acts of terror should know that we will uproot him."

"The Palestinian Authority now has a test. We expect that they will extradite and first of all help us to arrest these murderers of children, murders of women...We will not let up until we catch them," Netanyahu said.
Israel captured and occupied the West Bank and Gaza Strip in the 1967 Middle East war.
Today more than 130,000 Jewish settlers live amidst two million Palestinians in the territories where the PLO hopes eventually to establish an independent state.
Palestinians have said Netanyahu's lifting of a Jewish settlement building freeze imposed by the centre-left government he ousted in May elections could torpedo the Middle East peace process.
